info.title: Box Platform API
info.description: [Box Platform](https://developer.box.com) provides functionality to provide access to content stored within [Box](https://box.com). It provides endpoints for basic manipulation of files and folders, management of users within an enterprise, as well as more complex topics such as legal holds and retention policies.

post.description:
Initiates a Document Split job for the supplied source file. The job runs
asynchronously; clients can poll the returned job ID to track progress.

All split-specific input lives under `split_input`. When
`split_input.split_type` is `manual`, provide
`split_input.split_definition` (continuous page ranges; `version` may be
omitted or `v_1`). When `split_input.split_type` is `page_selection`,
provide `split_input.page_selection` (non-linear page segments; `version`
may be omitted or `v_2`). `split_input.prompt` must not be provided for
either of those variants. When `split_input.split_type` is `smart`,
`split_input.prompt` is required and neither
`split_input.split_definition` nor `split_input.page_selection` must be
provided.

split_input.prompt: Split this contract into one file per signed section.

post.description:
Runs a query to discover Box items using a logical predicate, similar to a SQL
WHERE clause. The predicate can filter across multiple metadata templates and
item fields in a single request. Results can be sorted, paginated with markers,
and shaped with fields so each entry includes additional item or metadata
attributes.

This is the item-retrieval endpoint in the Query API (version 2026.0). Unlike
the [Metadata Query API](https://developer.box.com/reference/post-metadata-queries-execute-read),
it is not limited to a single metadata template or to files and folders. For
totals and grouped metrics over the same predicates, use
[Query Insights](https://developer.box.com/reference/v2026.0/post-query-insights)
instead of paging through every matching item.

For predicate syntax, parameters, examples, pagination behavior, and error
codes, see the
[Box Query guide](https://developer.box.com/guides/query/box-query). For shared
response schemas, including Query results and result entries, see
[Query resources](https://developer.box.com/reference/v2026.0/query-resources).

200.description: Returns a paginated list of items matching the query.

400.description:
Returned when the query could not be parsed, the request body fails schema
validation, a referenced scope is not valid, or an unexpected JSON type was
provided.

401.description:
Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header is
missing, not valid, or expired.

403.description:
Returned when the query matched too many items, or too many inaccessible
items, to be processed.

404.description:
Returned when a referenced metadata template or item does not exist, or the
user does not have access to it.

429.description: Returned when the enterprise exceeds the allowed request rate.

500.description: Returned when an unexpected server error occurs while processing the query.

post.description:

post.description:
Accepts a spreadsheet of path mappings, already stored in Box, and replaces
the job's path mappings.
A file that is not a mapping workbook, or that exceeds the size or row
limits (10 MiB Box download limit; 100,000 mapping rows), returns `400`
synchronously and leaves the job unchanged.

ShuttleJob.description:
A standard representation of a shuttle job. A shuttle job describes a
migration of content from a source system into Box, including its current
state, mapping-preparation state, and mapping configuration.

id.description: The unique identifier for the shuttle job.

state.description:
The current state of the shuttle job. This is an open string whose set
of values is expected to grow; the currently documented values include
`created`, `started`, `stopped`, `completed`, `failed`, `invalid`, and
`unknown`. Clients should treat any value they do not recognize as
`unknown`.

mapping_state.description:
The current mapping-preparation state of the job. This is an open string
whose set of values is expected to grow; the currently documented values
include `awaiting_path_mapping`, `importing_paths`,
`paths_import_rejected`, `paths_invalid`, `paths_ready`,
`scanning_source`, `source_scan_failed`, `source_scan_out_of_date`,
`awaiting_subject_mapping`, `importing_subjects`,
`subjects_import_rejected`, `mapping_complete`, `building_map`,
`map_build_failed`, `map_out_of_date`, and `ready`.
`paths_import_rejected` means the last path-mapping spreadsheet was
rejected or failed and the path mappings have not been changed since;
it clears on the next import or the next manual path-mapping change.
`subjects_import_rejected` means the last subject-mapping spreadsheet
was rejected or failed and the subject mappings have not been changed
since; it clears on the next import or the next manual subject-mapping
change.
